pool.text: If \( \sqrt{2x + 7} = x + 2 \), what is the real solution for \( x \)?

pool.exam_archetype: Probability, Conditional Probability & Two-Way Tables — Non-Routine Synthesis & Past-Paper Challenge
pool.sol: Square both sides: \( 2x + 7 = (x + 2)^2 = x^2 + 4x + 4 \). Rearrange into standard form: \( x^2 + 2x - 3 = 0 \). Factor: \( (x + 3)(x - 1) = 0 \implies x = -3 \) or \( x = 1 \). Check for extraneous solutions: for \( x = -3 \), \( \sqrt{2(-3)+7} = \sqrt{1} = 1 \neq -3 + 2 = -1 \) (extraneous). For \( x = 1 \), \( \sqrt{2(1)+7} = 3 = 1 + 2 = 3 \) (valid). Thus \( x = 1 \).
